Koan 0.1.15

  • Icons for sites you haven’t opened on this Mac. A tab, pinned tab, essential or bookmark that arrived by sync, or from another device’s list, used to show a blank icon until you opened it here. Koan now asks the site itself for its icon while the row is on screen: a request with no cookies, never to an icon service, never for private windows, and once per site. Settings ▸ Privacy has a switch for it.
  • Clear History also forgets which sites were asked for an icon.

Koan 0.1.14

  • What’s New, redesigned. This page now opens once after each update, with every release dated and the ones you haven’t seen marked as new. Settings ▸ Updates has a switch for it, and Help ▸ What’s New in Koan opens it any time.
  • A Glance opened as a tab takes clicks again. After Open as Tab or Open in Split View, the page could stop responding to clicks and typing until Koan was quit. Koan also now checks, whenever a tab settles, that its page can take a click, and repairs it if not.
  • Websites see the light or dark you asked for. Sites that follow your Mac’s appearance could get stuck in light mode in Dark Mode, because Koan had judged them light-only. A page is now told only what you chose: the site’s setting, the workspace’s, or the default in Settings.
  • ⌘S shows and hides the sidebar (compact mode), as in Arc and Zen. Save Page As… moves to ⌃⌘S. Shortcuts you’ve customised are kept.

Koan 0.1.13

  • Pasting an image into a GitHub comment works. Smart dashes and smart quotes are now off in web pages, as in Safari. Before, Koan turned the -- in text a page inserted into a dash, so GitHub never found its "Uploading…" placeholder and the image never appeared. Any site that inserts text and looks for it again is fixed the same way.
  • Typing in Pages. Settings ▸ Pages has a new group: check spelling while typing (now on, as in Safari), grammar, automatic correction, smart quotes, smart dashes, text replacement and smart links. A change applies to pages that are already open.
  • Koan can no longer lock up behind a menu nobody can see. When another app pressed one of Koan's menus through accessibility while Koan was in the background, macOS left Koan waiting inside a menu that was never drawn, and no click or key reached it. Koan now ends such a menu within a few seconds. A menu you can see is never closed.

Koan 0.1.12

  • Local files open. An HTML file opened from Finder, from another app, with open or with File ▸ Open File… now renders. Before, it loaded for ever on a blank page. Koan remembers the file, so reloading, relaunching and a pinned tab for it keep working.
  • A file Koan isn't allowed to read says so. macOS only lets Koan open files you choose, so a typed or pasted file address that it can't read now shows a page that explains this, with a Choose File… button, instead of a spinner. A folder's address shows its contents.
  • Pages with files beside them. When a local page's styles, scripts or images are in a folder Koan hasn't been given, a small bar on the page offers Allow Folder…, once per folder.
  • A website still can't link to, open or embed a file on your Mac.
  • Quitting works even when Koan is stuck: it now ends by itself after ten seconds if it can't finish quitting normally.

Koan 0.1.11

  • A Glance moves into what it becomes. Open as Tab grows the card onto the page until it is the tab. Open in Split View sends the card to its pane while the page under it moves into the other. Close shrinks it back toward the link it came from. Each is one motion of the same page: nothing reloads, and what was playing keeps playing.
  • Opening a Glance is smoother, with a shorter worst frame than before, and choosing Split no longer stalls for a moment on heavy pages.
  • With Reduce Motion on, each of these is a short cross-fade instead.

Koan 0.1.10

  • The now playing card minimizes. The chevron on the card folds it into a slim pill with the artwork, the title and play / pause; click the pill for the full controls again. Both show playback as a brush stroke that follows the live state: it draws along as the track plays, rests when paused, and finishes with a small flourish when the track ends.
  • Several things playing at once each get a card. The most recent is the full card and the others stack above it as pills; past three, a line above them says how many more are playing and opens the rest.
  • Close a card you don't want. The ✕ on a card puts it away without stopping the sound. It comes back the next time you visit that tab and leave it again.
  • Much less work while audio plays. The speaker icon on a playing tab used to redraw the whole sidebar many times a second, which could cost around 40% of a core for as long as anything played. It no longer animates, and Koan now sits idle while music plays in the background.

Koan 0.1.9

  • Saved logins belong to a space. A login can be kept to one container, to the default one, or offered everywhere. In a workspace with its own container Koan offers that container's logins first, then the ones kept everywhere, and never another container's, so a work space doesn't offer your personal account for the same site. New logins are saved for the space you're in (the prompt lets you choose Everywhere). The Passwords window shows each login's container, filters by it and moves logins between them. Everything saved before this version is offered everywhere, as it was.
  • Import passwords from another browser. Koan ▸ Import Passwords… reads a profile of Chrome, Arc, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi, Ardia or another Chromium browser straight into the container you pick. macOS asks you to allow Koan to use that browser's key from your keychain; only you can start it. A CSV can go into a chosen container too.
  • Import from Ardia. File ▸ Import From Browser… brings each Ardia space in as a workspace with its own container: tiles become essentials, pinned tabs stay pinned with their names, pinned groups become folders, and bookmarks and history come too. It adds to what you have, takes a backup first, and running it again adds nothing twice.
  • One Glance setting for the click. "⌘-click opens a Glance" from 0.1.8 is gone: the "Open links in a Glance with" menu already offers ⌘-Click, and if you had the switch on, the menu is set to ⌘-Click for you. With ⌘-Click chosen, middle-click and ⇧⌘-click still open tabs.
  • A page can no longer open a Glance by itself, or use a faked ⌘-click to open background tabs; only your own clicks do.

Koan 0.1.8

  • Open links in a Glance by default. Two new switches in Settings ▸ Tabs ▸ Glance, both off until you turn them on. Open new-tab links in a Glance: a link the page would open in a new tab shows in a Glance over the page instead. ⌘-click opens a Glance: ⌘-click shows the link in a Glance instead of a background tab; middle-click and ⇧⌘-click still open tabs. Sign-in, payment and other pop-up windows open as they always did, and your routes still decide which workspace a link belongs to.
  • Agents can't touch your clipboard. Anything done through agent control (Koan's own Copy commands, copy and paste in pages and fields) now uses a clipboard of its own. Yours is read and changed only by what you do yourself.

Koan 0.1.7

  • The page moves with the sidebar. Turning compact mode on or off, or collapsing the sidebar to icons, used to slide the sidebar and then snap the page to its new width. The page's edge now follows the sidebar's edge the whole way, its content reflowing as it goes, and it is faster with hundreds of tabs than the snap was.
  • Routes that keep a site out of a workspace. Settings ▸ Tabs ▸ Routing has a second list, Never Open: "github.com never in Personal". A matching link opened from that workspace goes to one you choose, or to the last workspace you used that it may open in. The tab menu's Add Route for Domain offers it too. Tabs already open stay where they are.
  • Picture in picture works. The sidebar's picture in picture button did nothing and could leave the video black when you came back to the tab. The floating window was being blocked by the Mac's sandbox for every site, not only YouTube. It now opens from a background tab, and if it ever can't, the video stays in the page and Koan says why.
  • History on Back and Forward, kinds of reload on Reload. Right-click, or click and hold, Back or Forward for that tab's history. The same on Reload offers Reload, Reload From Origin (⌥⌘R) and Reload Without Content Blockers, which turns blocking off for that one load.
  • Inspect Element. With Settings ▸ Advanced ▸ Web Inspector on, Inspect Element is in the page's right-click menu, as it should have been.
  • Glance's buttons no longer shift their icons when you point at them.

Koan 0.1.6

  • Sync, through your own iCloud. Settings ▸ Sync is off until you turn it on. With it on, your workspaces, pinned tabs, folders, essentials and bookmarks are the same on every Mac signed in to your Apple Account. History and a list of each Mac's open tabs are separate switches, off to begin with; Library ▸ Other Devices shows what's open elsewhere. Private windows, passwords and website data never sync. Koan has no servers of its own: the data sits in your iCloud, where only you can read it. The welcome flow offers the switch to new installs.
  • When sync can't run, it says why. Not signed in to iCloud, iCloud Drive off, storage full, no network: each has its own sentence in Settings ▸ Sync instead of an error code.
  • Compact mode with hundreds of tabs. Sliding the sidebar in and out had become slower in 0.1.5 for workspaces of several hundred tabs. It is smooth again: about a third less time per frame at 300 tabs.
  • Saved logins and AutoFill move to a newer keychain. The first launch of this version moves Koan's saved logins, AutoFill details and live-folder token from the login keychain to the Mac's data-protection keychain. Nothing to do, and nothing should ask for a password.
  • Bookmarks arriving by sync keep their dates, so sorting by date added is the same on every Mac.
